**Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 61, verses 9–12:**

Allah the Exalted says:

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ ﴿You should believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.﴾ ﴿He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great achievement.﴾

This is a confirmation of the matter of the message and a strengthening of its support, as a person says of a matter he affirms and reinforces: "I did it," meaning: whoever is able to oppose it, let him oppose it. The "Messenger" referred to is Muhammad (ﷺ). His words, ﴿over all religion﴾, are a term that is suitable for generality, and the meaning may be: that no place will remain in which there is a religion other than Islam. This will not occur except at the descent of 'Isa (peace be upon him), as said by Abu Hurayrah and Mujahid. It may also be that the meaning is: that He make it prevail until no religion exists except that Islam is more manifest than it, and this has already been and has come to pass.

Then the Exalted encouraged the believers and urged them to jihad by means of this transaction which He has explained, namely that a person gives his self and his wealth and takes in exchange the Garden of eternity. The majority of the reciters read "tunjikum" with a light nun and a kasra on the jim without doubling. Ibn 'Amir alone, al-Hasan, al-A'raj, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read "tunajjikum" with a fatha on the nun and a doubled jim. His words, ﴿You should believe﴾ (*tu'minūna*), are in the form of a report but their meaning is a command, that is, "Believe!" In the Mushaf of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, it reads: "a painful [punishment]. Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive." His words, ﴿You should believe﴾ (*tu'minūna*), are a verb in the nominative case, its estimated reading being: "That is because you believe." Al-Akhfash said it is an explicative apposition (*'atf bayān*) to "transaction" (*tijāra*). Al-Mubarrad said it has the meaning of "Believe!" as an imperative, and for this reason "yaghfir" came in the jussive. His words, ﴿That﴾ (*dhalikum*), refer to jihad and belief. The word "khayr" (best) here may be comparative, so the meaning is "better than every deed," and it may be a statement that this is good in its own essence and nature.

The jussive "yaghfir" (He will forgive) is in response to an implied command in "tu'minūna," or to the exhortation and command contained in His words, ﴿shall I guide you﴾. This is the view al-Farra' took. It is reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he read "yughfilukum" with the ra' assimilated into the lam, but Sibawayh does not permit this. His words, ﴿and pleasant dwellings﴾ (*wa masakin*), are coordinated with "gardens" (*jannat*). "Pleasantness of dwellings" means their spaciousness and beauty; it was also said that their pleasantness is the knowledge that their state is everlasting.

The judge Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

This is the correct view. And what pleasantness is there with perishing and death?

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 61, verse 13–14:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified:

﴿And another [favour] you love: help from Allah and a near victory. So give good tidings to the believers.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my helpers for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are helpers of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: "wa-ukhrā" (and another). Al-Akhfash said: it is in the place of a genitive, in coordination with "tijāratin" (a commerce). This is an unsettled view; some people refuted it and others argued for it, but the correct position is its weakness, because this "another" is not among the things that were indicated; rather, it is among what is given as a price and recompense for faith and for striving with one's self and wealth. Al-Farrā' said: "wa-ukhrā" is in the place of the nominative. Some people said: "ukhrā" is in the place of the accusative, by an implied verb, as if He, exalted be He, said: He will forgive your sins, admit you into gardens, and grant you another [favour], which is the help and the near victory. Ibn Abī 'Abla read: "naṣran mina Allāhi wa-fatḥan" with the accusative in both. He, exalted be He, described it as something souls love, insofar as it is immediate in this world, and the soul has been entrusted with loving what is immediate; so in this there is encouragement. Then He strengthened it with His saying: ﴿and give good tidings to the believers﴾. These expressions are in the utmost conciseness and brilliance of meaning.

Then He, exalted be He, urged the believers to give help, and He assigned to them this title, although custom had restricted it to the Aws and the Khazraj, and Allah, exalted be He, named them by it. Ibn Kathīr, Nāfi', Abū 'Amr, al-A'raj and 'Īsā read "anṣāran" with tanwīn, "lillāh" (for Allah). The rest, al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī read it with the genitive construction. In the reading of 'Abd Allāh: "antum anṣāru Allāh" (you are the helpers of Allah).

Then He, exalted be He, set forth the example of people who hastened when they were called, namely the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn), and the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn) are the pure companions of the prophets, peace be upon them. They were so named because he (the one chosen) repeated their selection and their purification; likewise the repetition of the imagining of the disciple (ḥawāriyy). The two words derive from "al-ḥawar" (whiteness). It was said: they were so named for the whiteness of their garments, and they were launderers who helped 'Īsā, peace be upon him. Their name became in use until the helper and supporter was called ḥawāriyy. The Prophet ﷺ said: "My disciple (ḥawāriyy) is al-Zubayr." The division of the factions of the Children of Israel was over the matter of 'Īsā, peace be upon him. Qatādah said: the disbelieving faction consisted of three groups: the Ya'qūbiyya, who said: he is Allah; the Isrā'īliyya, who said: he is the son of Allah; and the Nasṭūriyya, who said: he is a god, and his mother is a god, and Allah is the third of them. Exalted is Allah, glorified be He, far above what they say, a great exaltation.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾. It was said: that refers to Muhammad ﷺ, and after an interval following the raising of 'Īsā, peace be upon him, Allah, exalted be He, returned the turn to those who believed in him, so they overcame the disbelievers who killed his companion upon whom the likeness was cast. It was also said: that refers to Muhammad ﷺ; the believer in 'Īsā, peace be upon him, became dominant by his belief in Muhammad ﷺ, because no one believes truly in 'Īsā, peace be upon him, except that within that belief is belief in Muhammad ﷺ, since he was given good tidings of him and urged toward him. It was also said: the believers had long been dominant by the proof, even though they remained scattered in the lands, overcome in the apparent life of this world. Mujāhid, Ḥumayd, al-A'raj and Ibn Muḥaysin read: "fa-ayyadnā" with a light yā' and an extended alif.

The commentary of Surah [al-Ṣaff] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
